items.summary: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 • Revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago • Data Center revenue of $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year ago • Vera Rubin NVL72, the most versatile and advanced computing platform ever built, has shipped SANTA CLARA, Calif.—Nov. 17, 2026― NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today reported revenue for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, of $115.8 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and up 103% from a year ago. For the quarter, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins were 74.8% and 74.9%, respectively. GAAP and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $2.70 and $2.68, respectively. “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” said Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of NVIDIA. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.” In September 2026, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors approved an increase of $150 billion to the company’s share repurchase authorization, without expiration. During the third quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA returned $28.1 billion to shareholders in the form of shares repurchased and cash dividends. As of the end of the third quarter, the company had approximately $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization. NVIDIA will pay its next quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share on December 23, 2026, to all shareholders of record on December 2, 2026. items.summary: NEWS RELEASE Contact Carolyn Guss AMD Communications corporate.pressinquiry@amd.com Liz Stine AMD Investor Relations investor.relations@amd.com AMD Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results AMD delivers record quarter as Data Center segment revenue grows 97% year-over-year, driven by record sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs SANTA CLARA, Calif. ― November 3, 2026 ― AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Third quarter revenue was $13.4 billion, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.8 billion, net income was $2.4 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.46. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 56%, operating income was $3.9 billion, net income was $3.5 billion and diluted earnings per share was $2.09. “We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year,” said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. “Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and ‘Venice’ production. With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years.” “Third quarter revenue grew 45% year-over-year to a record $13.4 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 74%, demonstrating the significant operating leverage in our business model as our Data Center business drives scale,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our fourth-quarter outlook reflects accelerating revenue and earnings growth, driven by strong demand across our Data Center portfolio.” 1 GAAP Quarterly Financial Results Q3'26 Q3'25 Y/Y Q2'26 Q/Q Revenue ($M) $13,377 $9,246 Up 45% $11,536 Up 16% Gross profit ($M) $7,210 $4,780 Up 51% $6,203 Up 16% Gross margin 54% 52% Up 2 ppts 54% Flat Operating expenses ($M) $4,378 $3,510 Up 25% $4,213 Up 4% Operating income ($M) $2,832 $1,270 Up 123% $1,990 Up 42% Operating margin 21% 14% Up 7 ppts 17% Up 4 ppts Net income ($M) $2,428 $1,24

items.summary: AMAZON.COM ANNOUNCES THIRD QUARTER RESULTS Operating income was $28.1 billion and operating margin was 13.9%—Amazon’s highest operating margin ever AWS net sales increased 39.3%—its fastest growth in nearly five years—to a $184 billion annualized revenue run rate SEATTLE—(BUSINESS WIRE) October 29, 2026—Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026. • Net sales increased 12% to $201.9 billion in the third quarter, compared with $180.2 billion in third quarter 2025. Excluding the $0.9 billion unfavorable impact from year-over-year changes in foreign exchange rates throughout the quarter, net sales increased 13% compared with third quarter 2025. As a reminder, Prime Day timing shifted this year, with the event occurring in Q2 for most large countries. In 2025, Prime Day occurred entirely in Q3. Excluding this shift, third quarter year-over-year growth would have been approximately 400 basis points higher. • North America segment sales increased 6% year-over-year to $112.9 billion. • International segment sales increased 5% year-over-year to $43.1 billion, or increased 8% excluding changes in foreign exchange rates. • AWS segment sales increased 39% year-over-year to $46.0 billion. • Operating income increased to $28.1 billion in the third quarter, compared with $17.4 billion in third quarter 2025. • North America segment operating income was $8.7 billion, compared with $4.8 billion in third quarter 2025. • International segment operating income was $1.6 billion, compared with $1.2 billion in third quarter 2025. • AWS segment operating income was $17.8 billion, compared with $11.4 billion in third quarter 2025. • Net income decreased to $20.7 billion in the third quarter, or $1.89 per diluted share, compared with $21.2 billion, or $1.95 per diluted share, in third quarter 2025. items.summary: Microsoft Announces First Quarter Results REDMOND, Wash. — October 28, 2026 — Microsoft Corp. today announced the following results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year: • Revenue was $92.3 billion and increased 19% • Operating income was $45.9 billion and increased 21% (up 22% in constant currency) • Net income was $36.6 billion and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $36.4 billion and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis • Diluted earnings per share was $4.92 and increased 32% on a GAAP basis, and was $4.89 and increased 18% (up 19% in constant currency) on a non-GAAP basis • Non-GAAP results exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI, explained in the Non-GAAP Definition section below “We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack,” said Satya Nadella, chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft. “By helping organizations build and own their own intelligence, and earning trust through agent safety and security, we are translating our innovation into growing adoption and real-world impact across every industry.” “We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year,” said Amy Hood, executive vice president and chief financial officer of Microsoft. “Results exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income, and earnings per share.” The following table adjusts for the impact from investments in OpenAI and reconciles our financial results reported in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) to non-GAAP financial results. items.summary: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif. – October 28, 2026 – Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOG, GOOGL) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. • Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 25% to $127.6 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 13th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth. • Google Services revenues increased 11% to $96.3 billion, led by 12% growth in Google Search & other with the year-over-year Search query growth rate the highest it has been in the last five years. • Google Cloud delivered record growth as revenues increased 103% to $30.7 billion, led by strong growth in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, as well as core GCP services. TPU systems sales were also a meaningful contributor to revenue growth. • Consolidated Alphabet operating income increased 30% and operating margin was 31.8%. • Net income available to common stockholders was $26.2 billion and EPS was $2.12. Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, said: “We had a strong quarter and are now on a half-trillion dollar revenue run rate. Our deep full stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with Alphabet revenues growing 25% year-over year. Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years. Google Cloud revenues grew 103%, powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions. We’re also seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers. Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon are now leading at the frontier. Overall, our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times what we processed a year ago. On top of that, the Gemini app has reached one billion users—making it the fastest-growing product in Google’s history—and we surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials.
